pins.title: Calorie tracking tips: why under-counting beats overeating as the real problem
pins.description: Most people who think they are overeating are actually under-counting. The calories that go missing are the handful while cooking, the last third of someone else's plate, and the oil the pan absorbed. Photo based food logging catches the whole plate at once. Calorie tracking tips for people who keep quitting. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting
pins.alt_text: You are not overeating, you are under-counting

pins.title: Guess the calories: what a salmon, green beans and crab cake dinner really costs
pins.description: A full dinner plate came to 485 calories and 42g of protein. Most people guess high, and they guess wrong on the same item every time. pins.title: 4 foods people always underestimate when counting calories
pins.description: The foods people misjudge are almost never the obvious ones. They are the sides, the cooking oil, and anything eaten standing up in the kitchen. pins.title: Why calorie tracking fails on day 4, and how to get past it
pins.description: Almost nobody quits tracking on day one. They quit on day four, when one meal is awkward to log and skipping it is easier. The fix is not more willpower, it is making the awkward meal take five seconds. Habit tips for anyone who has started tracking food and stopped. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting
pins.alt_text: Day four is when tracking dies

pins.title: Tracking food badly beats tracking nothing: consistency over accuracy
pins.description: The people who get results from food logging are not the accurate ones, they are the ones who never stopped. A rough estimate you logged is worth more than a perfect number you skipped. Calorie tracking for beginners who are tired of starting over. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting

pins.title: Calorie quiz: which item on this plate is 140 calories?
pins.description: Four foods on one dinner plate. The smallest one by weight turned out to be the second largest by calories. Test how well you estimate portions, then see the real itemised breakdown from a photo scan. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting
pins.alt_text: The crab cake question

pins.title: Why your weekend ruins your calorie tracking week
pins.description: Weekday eating is repeatable so it is easy to log. Weekend eating is social, unmeasured and cooked by someone else, which is exactly why it goes untracked. Two unlogged days is not two missing days, it is a whole week you cannot read. Weekend food tracking tips. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting
pins.alt_text: Why the weekend breaks your week

pins.title: How to track protein without weighing food or looking anything up
pins.description: Protein is the macro people misjudge most, usually downward. One photo of a dinner plate itemised it at 42 grams across four foods against a 135 gram daily target. No food scale, no database search, no mental arithmetic. High protein tracking made simple. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting
pins.alt_text: One photo, four foods, 42g protein

pins.title: The log of shame spiral: why one missed meal ends your food diary
pins.description: Nobody quits food logging because the food was bad. They quit because one unlogged meal made the day incomplete, and an incomplete day makes the whole week feel pointless. The meal you do not want to log is the exact one worth logging. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting
pins.alt_text: The log of shame spiral

pins.title: What happens when you stop estimating calories and start reading them
pins.description: The plate looked like 700 calories. It was 485. Nothing about the meal changed, only whether the number came from a guess or from a scan. pins.title: Guess the protein, not the calories: a harder macro quiz

pins.title: Food tracking is a receipt, not a diet
pins.description: A receipt does not tell you off, it tells you what happened. People who last at calorie tracking read the number the way they read a bank statement, then adjust. pins.title: 3 ways to log a meal badly and still get results
pins.description: There is no version of food logging so sloppy that it loses to not logging at all. Photograph it and fix the details later, log the closest match, or log half of it now. All three keep your week readable. Calorie tracking tips for real life. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting

pins.title: AI calorie estimates are not precise, and that is the point
pins.description: Estimates get treated as a weakness in calorie tracking apps. They are the feature. A precise number you never write down is worth nothing next to a rough one you log every day, because only the trend has ever changed how anyone eats. #CalorieTracking #FoodTracker #MacroTracking #HealthyHabits #CalorieCounting

pins.title: The cooking oil calories that never make it into your food log
pins.description: Cooking oil is the most commonly missed number in home cooking, because it goes into the pan before the food does and never feels like eating.
